newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes lower despite budget vote.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes lower despite budget vote.

text.p: The PX50 and RPIX indices on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) both fell on Thursday despite the passing of the first reading of the 1997 state budget in the Czech Parliament late on Wednesday.

While foreign exchange markets followed the news by pushing the Czech crown higher, equities investors were less impressed. The PX50 fell 0.5 percent to 545.3 and the RPIX dropped by the same amount to 1,105.

"I think the budget first reading passing is too weak a signal but it is definitely positive. There are still structural problems to be solved before investors get more confident in this market," said Karel Ruzicka of ING Barings.

Like many traders in the Czech capital markets Ruzicka said the lack of transparency and the absence of strong regulations protecting minority shareholder's rights was a key problem which would not go away until firm action was taken.
The lack of a smoothly functioning equities market has been especially worrying to foreign investors who are heavily involved in trading in major issues.
On the PSE on Thursday all but one of the top four most heavily capitalised issues fell.
Komercni Banka lost 23 crowns to 2,215, CEZ fell two crowns to 1,013, SPT Telecom dropped 34 crowns to 3,231 with Ceska Sporitelna the only gainer, rising four crowns to 319.
Together, the above four issues account for around 45 percent of the PX50 index's total capitalisation.
